**Pantone “Sky Blue”**

| Pantone Code | Description / Notes |
|--------------|---------------------|
| **Pantone 290 C** | Officially named *“Sky Blue.”* It’s the classic light‑to‑mid‑tone blue most people think of when picturing a clear daytime sky. |

> **Why Pantone 290 C?**  
> - In the Pantone Matching System (PMS) it sits at about 20% cyan, 0% magenta, 0% yellow, with a very low black level—exactly what gives it its airy, cloud‑like quality.  
> - Designers often use it as a neutral background because it doesn’t compete strongly with other hues while still adding subtle depth.  

### Other Common “Sky‑Like” Pantones

If you’re looking for slightly lighter or brighter options, consider:

| Pantone | Shade name | Typical feel |
|---------|------------|---------------|
| **Pantone 291 C** | Light Sky Blue | Very pale, almost pastel tone |
| **Pantone 292 C** | Bright Sky Blue | Slightly deeper, more saturated than 290 C |
| **Pantone 299 C** | Ultra-Light Blue | Near-white, used for crisp highlights |

These alternatives can help fine‑tune your design if the exact “classic sky blue” isn’t quite right for your project.
